title: Input to the `knowledge.generateMigrationDraft` MCP tool
description:
What a caller may send to `knowledge.generateMigrationDraft`, the operations write-intent tool (ADR-0032 decision 3). SEC-12 validates every call against this file before it reaches application code, in the MCP server middleware (ADR-0031 decision 2). The tool takes a caller-authored migration document and lands it as a proposal through `ProposalService.draft_from_document`, reaching no approved-state write (ADR-0013).

**The v1 operation set is enforced in the service, not here.** The document is checked against the published migration schema and the closed v1 operation set inside `ProposalService.draft_from_document` (ADR-0032 decision 3): it admits ten of the fourteen `OperationKind` members and refuses `createItem`/`upsertRevision` to `knowledge.proposeChange` and `changeSensitivity`/`restoreItem` to the CLI. This boundary schema constrains only the *envelope* — that a document object and an evidence object arrive — so an agent that reaches for a refused operation is redirected by the service rather than told which schema fields its incomplete operation is missing.

**There is no path, URI, or reference field (ADR-0032 decision 2).** No admitted operation names a `contentFile`, so this path lands no body and has no body path to contain; the proposal directory and migration filename are minted from ids the service chooses, never from caller text.

**Composition.** The context — `projectId`, and the optional `snapshotId`, `agentId` and `taskId` — arrives by `$ref` to `tool-context.schema.json`, closed with `unevaluatedProperties: false` (ADR-0031 decision 1). `projectId` is required by the referent and is not repeated here.

**Evidence is authoritative (ADR-0032 decision 4),** exactly as on `knowledge.proposeChange`: `evidence.agentId`/`evidence.taskId` are required and reach the proposal; a top-level context field that disagrees with its evidence counterpart is refused in the handler.

document.description: The migration document to land as a proposal. Its internal shape is validated against the published migration schema, and its operations against the v1 set, inside the service — this boundary constrains only that an object arrives. It is bounded by the middleware's structural limits (nesting, node count) and the transport body cap; a document larger or deeper than those is refused before it reaches the service.

evidence.description: Where the proposed change came from and why (ADR-0013 point 5). Provenance only. Authoritative for `agentId`/`taskId` (ADR-0032 decision 4).

agentId.description: Which agent drafted this. Required, and what reaches the evidence record.

taskId.description: The unit of work it came out of. Required.

model.description: The model identity that produced it. Required.

reasoning.description: Why the evidence supports the claim. Required.

local.description: Draft under .theurian/proposals-local/ instead (ADR-0028). Defaults to false.
